what_this_is: PRE-REGISTERED before the arm launches. A Terminal-Bench 2.1 arm served at 524,288 tokens via Qwen's official static YaRN at FACTOR 2.0 - the setting Qwen's own card prescribes for a 512k window, since they advise tuning factor to actual need rather than always using 4.0. The question: does the fidelity penalty measured at factor 4.0 (~1.03e-02 mean top-20 KLD, docs/46 s31/s34) scale DOWN with the factor?
why_a_subset: Credits are being deliberately drained rather than protected, so the arm runs on the tasks that actually discriminate instead of all 89. Running the full set would cost ~2x the time for the same signal, because 43 tasks resolved in BOTH the 262k and 1M arms and carry no information about the rope.
selection_rule: union of (a) the 45 twice-failed tasks in receipts/terminal-bench-2.1-attribution.json - every task that failed both stock-clock passes - and (b) the 13 tasks the 1M-YaRN arm LOST relative to 262k per receipts/tb21-1m-yarn-arm.json; then MINUS the 2 nested-virt qemu tasks, which are structurally unattemptable on a Jarvis VM; then MINUS one further exclusion below.

further_exclusion.reason: Pre-registered exclusion on DISK-SAFETY grounds, decided before launch and not after seeing a result. In the 1M arm this single task emitted a 1.6 GB asciinema recording plus a 545 MB tmux pane dump - 2.1 GB from one task, and 95 percent of all job-directory bytes. It has never resolved in any arm. Risking the driver's disk for a task that carries no rope signal is a bad trade.

arm_config.concurrency: C32 (8 shards x n=4, DP8's measured knee)
arm_config.serve_argv_shape: docker run --rm --name qwen38-dp8-512k --gpus all --ipc host -p 10.0.0.5:8000:8000 -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 -v /home/ubuntu/models:/models:ro -e VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 -e VLLM_EXL3_GRAPH_DECODE=1 -e VLLM_EXL3_PREFILL_RECONSTRUCT_M=128 -e VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 --entrypoint /opt/venv/bin/vllm vllm:gg-r34-tb21-sr1 serve /models/qwen38-hyd --served-model-name qwen38 --data-parallel-size 8 --quantization exl3 --quantization-config <as production> --hf-overrides {"text_config":{"rope_parameters":{"mrope_interleaved":true,"mrope_section":[11,11,10],"rope_type":"yarn","rope_theta":10000000,"partial_rotary_factor":0.25,"factor":2.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":262144}}} --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-cache-mode align --enable-prefix-caching --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"} --max-model-len 524288 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192

comparability.comparable_to: the 262k-native arm (56/89) and the 1M-YaRN arm (48/89) ON THE SHARED SUBSET ONLY - all three used C32-or-C16, 2x timeouts, the same image and the same default reasoning effort. The denominator here is the subset, never 89.
NOT_comparable_to: 44/89 best-of-2 stock clock (the published lower bound)
any leaderboard figure, because the agent timeout is non-stock
comparability.note: The 1M arm ran at C16 and this runs at C32, so contention differs; the 262k arm also ran C32. Where this arm is compared to 1M, the concurrency difference is stated.

attempt_caps_binding.abandon_if: fewer than 30 % of the pre-registered tasks have results after 2.5x the expected wall clock
attempt_caps_binding.rationale: owner set no balance floor and asked for value even if interrupted, so partial merges are the deliverable
